title: Level 1 (Beginner) - B-21
notes:
West leads the ♠Q against 4♥. South should not play dummy's ♠K. Against a suit contract, West would not lead the ♠Q if he also held the ♠A. On the given lie of the cards, South's play in spades does not matter. The defense will take 3 spade tricks and then play a club to South's ♣A.

South has 2 club losers to worry about. If South is fortunate, he can establish and enjoy North's diamonds to discard his losing clubs. South should win 2 heart tricks in the closed hand, making sure to preserve dummy's ♥Q. When hearts prove to be 3-2, half of the battle is over.

South now plays to the ♦A, cashes the ♦K, and trumps a diamond in his hand. When diamonds are 3-3, South can draw the last trump with dummy's ♥Q and play the good diamonds to discard his club losers.
